title: Post Neutron Irradiation Characterization of the Effects of Grain Size on Microstructural Evolution and Mechanical Properties in an FeCrAl Alloy
content: FeCrAl alloys with their enhanced corrosion resistance at elevated temperatures are being investigated with the prospective to replace Zr-based alloys in nuclear fuel cladding applications. Given that grain boundaries act as sinks for irradiation induced defects [1, 2], grain refinement including nanostructuring, which leads to increased grain boundary fraction, presents a potential means of improving irradiation resistance of such materials in a nuclear reactor environment. Samples of Kanthal D (Fe-21Cr-5Al) have been processed using multiple techniques of severe plastic deformation, more specifically equal-channel angular pressing and high-pressure torsion, to represent different grain sizes ranging from ∼75 nm to 40 µm. These samples were irradiated in the advanced test reactor (ATR) to a dose of 2 displacements per atom (DPA) at 300 °C and 500 °C. Through characterization including mechanical testing, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and atom probe tomography (APT), differences in irradiation damage effects including radiation-induced segregation relative to grain size and irradiation condition will be presented.
